# SR 26-2: what it means for Northmere Financial Group (fictional)

**For:** Priya Raman (fictional), Chief Audit Executive
**Trigger:** SR 26-2, Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management

## What changed
On April 17, 2026, the Federal Reserve, OCC and FDIC replaced SR 11-7 with SR 26-2, their revised guidance on model risk management.[1] It is aimed mainly at banking organizations with over $30 billion in total assets.[2] The guidance explicitly leaves generative and agentic AI out of scope: "Generative AI and agentic AI models are novel and rapidly evolving. As such, they are not within the scope of this guidance."[2]

## What it means for Northmere
- Northmere's US banking arm is in the size range the guidance targets (account record: US operations over $30B, fictional), so its traditional models will be measured against the refreshed expectations for inventory, validation and governance.[2]
- Northmere has agents in pilot on internal operations (account record, fictional). SR 26-2 does not cover them, so they will not be picked up by the model-risk program by default.[2]
- That leaves a question of ownership: which internal policy governs those agents, and who in audit tests it. The account record shows a risk committee is in place (fictional), which is the natural forum to assign it.

## Three questions your team could ask this quarter
1. Which of our AI agents are in production or pilot today, and are they tracked in any inventory, given SR 26-2 keeps them out of the model inventory?
2. For each agent action that touches a customer or a record, can we show who approved that class of action, what the agent did, and why?
3. Which internal policy, if not model-risk management, is the control framework for agentic AI, and who owns it?

## Sources
1. Federal Reserve, SR 26-2 cover letter: https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm
2. Federal Reserve, SR 26-2 guidance attachment (pp. 2–3): https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602a1.pdf
